Historical August climatology for the city shows average highs of 29–31 °C, with occasional spikes to 32–33 °C only under clear, calm, and drier conditions that are not currently anticipated.  

Recent model runs and observational trends have reinforced this picture, shifting trader consensus strongly toward 30 °C (77 % implied probability) while still allowing a meaningful but secondary chance for 31 °C (23.5 %). Higher thresholds remain improbable without an unexpected clearing trend or stronger offshore flow, scenarios not supported by the latest guidance.

Stronger El Niño conditions have elevated the seasonal baseline temperature anomaly, but today’s local convective regime remains the decisive short-term control on the observed maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus for Wellington on August 21, 2026, centers on a maximum of 13–14 °C, aligning with the market’s strong weighting toward those outcomes (63.5 % at 14 °C, 29.5 % at 13 °C).** August is climatologically cool in the capital, with long-term average daily highs near 12–13 °C; current guidance shows near-average conditions driven by a transient ridge of high pressure that limits strong southerly flow while allowing modest daytime warming under partly cloudy skies.

Official and ensemble forecasts from MetService, NIWA, and international models (GFS/ECMWF) converge on a daytime peak of 13 °C, with some runs reaching 14 °C if cloud cover thins earlier. Light winds, minimal precipitation after early sprinkles, and sea-surface temperatures around 11–12 °C support this narrow range; colder anomalies seen earlier in the month have eased. Resolution depends on the official maximum recorded at the primary station (typically Wellington Aero), so any late-model shift in timing of cloud or wind could nudge the outcome between the two leading bins. Traders appear to be pricing the tight scientific agreement and limited upside potential from current atmospheric setup.

These conditions, including increased cloud cover and scattered precipitation, limit solar heating compared with clearer recent days when Tokyo recorded 32.5–32.6°C. Typical August climatology features average highs around 30.9°C, but the current pattern of modest instability and higher humidity supports the market-implied clustering near 31°C. Model consensus remains tight, with limited upside risk above 33°C or downside below 29°C unless unexpected clearing occurs. Traders are weighting the latest JMA and ensemble guidance heavily, as the market will resolve on the official Tokyo station maximum once observations finalize.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance places Miami's August 21 high in the low-to-mid 90s, reflecting a persistent subtropical ridge and above-average sea surface temperatures that sustain heat despite occasional sea-breeze moderation. The recent heat wave, including a 100°F reading on August 18 that tied the all-time record, has elevated trader expectations, yet increasing thunderstorm chances and slightly cooler steering flow appear to cap extremes near 94°F. Model consensus favors 92–93°F as the most probable peak, consistent with climatological August averages near 89°F while accounting for current anomalies; later forecast updates from local NWS offices will refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.
